key_insight: A lightweight machine-learning interatomic potential learns from unary and binary systems to predict interactions in unseen ternary and quaternary metal alloys.
engineering_relevance: Targeted training could reduce the cost of developing transferable potentials for multi-element alloy simulations.
method: Use step-wise active learning to build a compact, diverse training dataset.
Train a general-purpose potential spanning Al, Sc, Ti, V, Cu, Zn, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta and W.
Extend to new elements through alchemical extrapolation using only unary data for each new element.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports transfer to unseen ternary and quaternary systems from unary and binary training data, but provides no numerical accuracy or runtime results.
watch_item: Validate accuracy for the intended alloy compositions and operating conditions before relying on transfer beyond the training data.
paper_title: Learning Between the Lines: Interaction Interpolation in a Multi Element Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
